title: Causal Effect Identifiability in Causal Abstractions: A Strict Hierarchy of Criteria
abstract: arXiv:2610.13520v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Identifying causal effects from observational data typically requires a fully specified causal graph, an assumption that is often unrealistic in complex or high-dimensional settings. Causal abstractions address this limitation by retaining only partial causal information, thereby defining equivalence classes of compatible causal graphs. In this paper, we study causal effect identifiability directly at the level of these graph collections, rather than at the level of individual causal diagrams. We formalize several notions of identifiability in this setting and organize them into a hierarchy that clarifies their relationships and differences. In particular, we establish that a causal effect may be identified over a collection of graphs without admitting a single causal derivation that holds uniformly across all compatible graphs. These results help reveal gaps and clarify ambiguities in the existing literature.

translated_title: 因果抽象中的因果效应可识别性：一个严格的标准层次结构
translated_abstract: 从观测数据中识别因果效应通常需要一个完全指定的因果图，这一假设在复杂或高维环境中往往不切实际。因果抽象通过仅保留部分因果信息来解决这一局限，从而定义了与之兼容的因果图的等价类。在本文中，我们直接在这些图集合的层面上研究因果效应的可识别性，而非在单个因果图的层面上进行研究。我们在这一设定下形式化了可识别性的若干概念，并将它们组织成一个层次结构，以阐明它们之间的关系与差异。特别地，我们证明了某个因果效应可能在一个图集合上是可识别的，却不存在一个在所有兼容图上一致成立的单一因果推导。这些结果有助于揭示现有文献中的空白，并澄清其中的模糊之处。
tldr: 本文在因果抽象所定义的图集合层面上研究因果效应可识别性，建立了各可识别性标准之间的严格层次结构，并证明一个效应可能在图集合上可识别，却不存在对所有兼容图一致成立的单一因果推导。
en_tdlr: This paper studies causal effect identifiability at the level of graph collections induced by causal abstractions, establishes a strict hierarchy among identifiability criteria, and proves that an effect can be identified over a collection of graphs without admitting a single causal derivation that holds uniformly across all compatible graphs.
